A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WarmServe. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated during the extensive restructuring.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original serving-latency measurements, prewarming experiments, ablations and workload-prediction results. Appendix A supplies additional TPOT distributions.

after.justification: Section 4 reports original serving experiments, ablations, workload predictions and a 512-GPU simulation. Appendix A retains additional experimental results.

M1.justification: The CSP correction changes from using N previous windows in v1 Eq. 3 to min(i,N) windows with corresponding normalization in v2 Eq. 2, altering predictions near day boundaries. The central placement rules, replica scores, KV-cache reservation and memory-switching procedure remain, including details relocated to Appendices B–D.

E1.justification: Prediction evaluation expands from AzureConv and AzureCode to include BurstGPT and ServeGen's m-small workload, substantially broadening the production workloads supporting predictability (v2 Sections 2.2 and 4.6). The existing Llama2 serving workloads remain; AzureCode serving results move to Appendix A.3.

E2.justification: SLLM-GPU and MuxServe remain the end-to-end comparators. V2 Section 4.5 and Table 3 add predictive autoscaling using the same workload predictor but without prewarming. This adds a distinct comparison method within the new simulation.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a 512-GPU simulation at alpha=0.5 and 320–800 RPS, extending evaluation beyond the original 16-GPU testbed. Table 2 also adds an already-running engine condition. The reported GPU specification changes from approximately 2K FP16 TFLOPS to 1K dense-FP16 TFLOPS; this does not establish hardware replacement or experimental reruns.

E4.justification: Diagnostic evidence is substantially revised: v2 adds a completely disabled-prewarming ablation and a simulation control testing whether prediction without prewarming suffices. It removes v1's startup-stage breakdown and weekday/weekend prediction-error analysis. The placement, proactive-prewarming and prediction-window ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or between-run error bars. Prediction errors and request-latency CDFs do not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds simulation results, including P99 TTFT of 0.38 s for WarmServe versus 4.42 s for predictive autoscaling at 800 RPS, plus new trace predictions and ablation results. Table 2 retains v1 Figure 8's startup endpoints but corrects stated speedups from 29.8–54.8× to 60.13–87.63× and adds 0.05 s warm-engine results. Intermediate startup-stage measurements and detailed prediction-error results are removed.

T1.justification: The CSP corrective-term definition changes its summation limit and denominator from N to min(i,N). Other substantive formulas, including replica scores and KV-cache reservation, remain equivalent. The new input/output formulations mostly restate existing mathematics; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The one-for-many prewarming contribution and headline 50.8× TTFT and 2.5× request-capacity claims remain. V2 explicitly claims joint placement/prewarming problem formulation as a contribution and narrows the prominently stated zero-overhead memory-switching claim to efficient or near-zero-overhead switching.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1 Section 7.4's discussion of limited historical coverage, worse weekend predictions and possible benefits from weekly periodicity. It adds explanations for predictive autoscaling's heavy-load failures and performance under suboptimal prediction windows. Existing AzureCode and GPU-sharing interpretations remain in Appendix A.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a public-code access statement and repository address, specifies seven historical days, and discloses the ablation's 25-RPS load and round-robin fallback. Much implementation information moves to Appendix D, but partial-layer loading/profiling, shared-memory notifications and the 64-CPU/2-TB host specifications are no longer documented. These omissions do not establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds works including Weaver, Aegaeon, Tangram, PipeBoost, Coral and P-LoRA, explicitly distinguishing adapter prefetching from full-model prewarming. Some earlier discussion and citations, including PipeSwitch and InfiniGen, disappear. The principal positioning around autoscaling, GPU sharing and serverless prewarming remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. Separate overview, worker, manager and implementation sections become a consolidated Method section with problem/input/output exposition. Detailed methods and many results move to Appendices A–D, while related work and the conclusion are compressed and acknowledgments and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the architecture diagram, replaces the startup-stage chart with Table 2, adds simulation Table 3 and creates multi-trace prediction panels. Retained experimental plots and method diagrams are relocated and resized throughout the appendices. The conference layout also substantially changes the visual organization.

improvement.justification: Four-trace prediction validation, the predictive-autoscaling control, the added no-prewarming ablation and corrected startup speedups strengthen the evidence and numerical consistency. The code-access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These gains are tempered by sparse simulation details and the loss of explicit prediction limitations and partial-layer implementation information, supporting a limited overall improvement.
